initial_scene: Robot-centered elevated view looking outward along the paired forearms toward a table. Brown paper bag lies open on the left, with a far handle extending behind the closed left hand. A pink peach with green leaf rests on the upper black shelf to the right; right hand is initially open near the fruit stand.

observed_sequence.observation: Left hand is already closed at the bag handle, whose visible cord disappears behind the hand. Bag is open. Right hand open below the upper shelf; peach remains on the shelf.
observed_sequence.confidence: high for visible arrangement; medium-high for occluded handle support

observed_sequence.observation: Right hand raises and reorients toward the peach with digits apart. Left hand retains its position and the handle has no visible disengagement.
Right front digit contacts/crosses the peach and opposing digits close around its body. Fruit remains at shelf height while grasp establishes. Left remains closed at handle.
observed_sequence.confidence: high for grasp; exact back-side fingertip contact occluded

observed_sequence.observation: Right hand raises peach; fruit and hand move together and peach clears the shelf. Left still holds handle without visible regrasp.

Right carries peach inward toward bag. Left raises the handle continuously: cord segment and far-wall attachment rise with hand, and the far bag wall lifts relative to the near wall. Right lowers peach through opening while its digits remain opposed around it.
observed_sequence.confidence: high for coordinated motion; exact left digit-handle interface occluded

observed_sequence.observation: Right hand and enclosed peach descend farther inside bag. Left retains raised handle. The inner paper surface is visible beneath fruit, but direct fruit-support contact is not established from projection alone.
observed_sequence.confidence: high for interior location and hand pose

observed_sequence.observation: Right digits spread, upper opposing digits separate from peach, and peach shifts down/left relative to hand and turns its leaf out of view. A front fingertip still overlaps peach in final frame, so complete contact loss is not established. Left retains raised handle; no withdrawal or subsequent settling is visible.
observed_sequence.confidence: high for opening and relative motion; uncertain for complete release

arm_hand_roles.right: Closes around peach body, bears it during shelf lift and transport, lowers it into bag, then opens digits around it. Complete release cannot be confirmed because final front fingertip overlaps fruit.
arm_hand_roles.left: Continuously holds/supports one bag handle from beginning, lifts handle and its attached bag wall during transport/insertion, retains it at final frame. No observed release or regrasp. Exact finger-handle pinch is hidden behind hand.
arm_hand_roles.coordination: Left moves handle/far wall to keep bag opening accessible while right independently bears and lowers peach. No hand-to-hand fruit transfer. Left never touches fruit, and no human assists.

anatomical_side_evidence.observation: The generation view looks forward from behind/above the robot forearms: both forearms originate at the bottom near the camera and extend outward across the table. The arm at the robot-centered lower right reaches to the shelf and is anatomical right; the opposing lower-left arm holds the bag and is anatomical left. Paired hand/forearm orientation supports this body-centered convention, rather than a front-facing reversal.
anatomical_side_evidence.limitation: Torso and shoulder attachments are outside the camera crop; the arm side assignment is based on visible paired forearm origins and the egocentric geometry, and agrees with but is not solely derived from the source instruction.

terminal_state: Peach lies within the visible bag opening, with right digits spreading around it and front fingertip still overlapping it. Left retains raised handle; the upper black shelf is empty. Complete release, transfer of weight to the bag interior, settling and right-hand withdrawal are not established.
uncertainties: Exact left-hand finger/handle contact is hidden behind its hand backplate; handle support is supported by continuous cord-to-hand proximity and coupled rise of handle attachment and bag wall. No rim pinch is visibly established.
At final frame the right front fingertip overlaps peach; complete release and absence of residual contact cannot be confirmed.
Peach-to-interior paper support and post-release settling cannot be established from the available depth/projection and ending.
Torso/shoulders are cropped out; anatomical naming follows visible paired forearm origins in the robot-centered outward-looking view.
